findings: As written this is direct observation/recall that leaves occur at different depths, with no path calculation or competing stopping constraints. Label easy or add a meaningful depth/leaf analysis before retaining medium.

The alternatives that depth counts every node and that every internal node has one child are remote from the tested unequal-leaf-depth distinction. Replace them with plausible balanced/full/complete-tree or edge-versus-node depth confusions.

The claims that classification trees forbid pure leaves and that impurity proves test leakage are not plausible rivals to a stopping explanation. Use competing stopping, inconsistent-label, sample-limit or split-improvement mechanisms instead.

All three wrong alternatives are sweeping zero-false-alarm, universal-axis or every-network superiority claims. A learner can select the sole measured qualification without understanding the source; use realistic limited-validation or deployment trade-offs.

The solution specifically calls this a synthetic classifier but cites only page 866, which gives the robot problem and motivation. Add the synthetic-generation premise on page 868, or remove that unsupported characterization from this exact solution.

Deleting label arrays, always producing a deeper tree, and adding prediction-time branches are implausible distractors for the pre/post-pruning distinction. Use realistic timing, validation-set and structural-operation confusions.

Plotting color maps and random_state as pruning penalties are obvious unrelated API controls. Contrast ccp_alpha with plausible actual growth controls or with the source reduced-error procedure, retaining the explicit dated external qualification.

Feature sorting, normalization and guaranteed perfect accuracy do not offer a close stratification misconception. Use realistic confusion between preserving proportions, equalizing counts, independently splitting labels, or oversampling.
This asks for the direct purpose of a named parameter, with no count or imbalanced-class reasoning. Relabel easy or introduce a genuine class-allocation application to justify medium.
The question compares the max_depth=3 code with the printed fitted depth-2 tree, but cites only page 871. Add page 873, which supplies the second premise and actual topology.

Pure-leaf maximum impurity and universal deeper-tree test improvement are not close alternatives to training-data instability. Replace at least these with realistic bias, observation-noise, seed-variation or fixed-model sensitivity distinctions.

Removing supervision and ensuring simultaneous zero training/test error are weak rivals to variance reduction. Use plausible ensemble motivations or failure mechanisms so the correct qualification is not the only credible option.
Per-node feature resampling is directly stated on page 877; this is easy parameter/procedure recall as written. A two-node candidate-subset trace would support medium.

Feature selection only after a leaf prediction or only on the held-out test set are implausible distractors. A fixed per-tree subset, fixed per-forest subset and independently resampled per-node subset are the useful distinctions.
The correct option relies on earlier variables X_tr/y_tr, but only page 880 is cited. Add page 871 so both code fragments involved in the comparison are available as exact source premises.

Claiming that classifiers cannot accept NumPy arrays or that tree count must equal training-row count makes the code-completeness answer too obvious. Use realistic undefined-name, aliasing, split and fit-signature mistakes.

The figure comparison depends on the earlier three-class fall experiment, but the only citation is the binary forest figure on page 881. Add page 866 or 868 to support the compared three-class premise.

The alternatives that every classification diagram uses identical data or a forest cannot display two features are implausible. Use believable dataset-identity, class-count and plotting-versus-model distinctions.

Fitting fewer trees by increasing their count, changing classification to regression, and automatic perfection after the class count are weak distractors. Contrast realistic computational, correlation, variance and test-score trade-offs.

Randomly choosing the number of target classes or relabeling held-out targets are not plausible sources of ordinary forest randomness. Use real distinctions between bootstrapping, feature subsampling, tie-breaking and deterministic seed reuse.

Page 882 gives an incorrect regression default and does not define floating max_features=1.0. This item uses the corrected API semantics without its own dated official-document qualification. Add that explicit premise, as Q060 already does, while keeping the source conflict visible.

Mixing train/test labels and standardizing each test row are unrelated evaluation/preprocessing errors rather than plausible consequences of tree scale invariance. Present comparable data-preparation choices involving scaling, encoding, invalid shapes and model requirements.

Nodes containing no parameters, exactly unchanged prediction cost for more trees, and universal inability to accept high dimensions are implausible absolutes. Replace with realistic memory, latency, parallelism or dimensionality trade-offs.

An extra tree proving a theorem, making tuning unnecessary, or proving a single tree never predicts correctly are straw-man alternatives. Use plausible distinctions between a reported empirical trend, supplied benchmark evidence and a universal guarantee.

Rejecting a tree because it is interpretable and treating an application list as safety validation are weak alternatives; the remaining wrong option is an unconditional production rule. Use realistic but incomplete model-selection criteria so the correct option is not the only sensible process.

This repeats Q020's central inference that a synthetic readable/example result does not establish universal robot safety. It adds no evaluated error pattern or changed reasoning demand. Replace this with a genuinely distinct source-bound evaluation or full pipeline analysis, rather than another universal-guarantee rejection.

All wrong choices assert universal zero error, a nonexistent real-world safety trial or universal perfect classification of Gaussian data. Use credible dataset/split/generalization inferences when replacing the duplicate angle.

coverageGaps.finding: max_leaf_nodes limits total terminal nodes, distinct from max_depth and minimum child samples. No current question tests this explicitly printed growth control. Add a constrained topology or growth-choice item rather than another general pruning definition.

The actual source post-pruning rule replaces a subtree by a leaf when pruning-set error does not increase, including equality. Q027 only names timing and Q028 corrects the API claim; neither tests the stated error comparison. Add a small before/after pruning-set example, clearly distinguishing this reduced-error description from ccp_alpha cost-complexity pruning.

The best-split criterion is described, but Q012/Q013 evaluate one unsplit leaf and Q038 only root Gini. No item actually chooses between candidate splits using their child errors and sample weighting. Add a meaningful multi-step split comparison with all required criterion definitions supplied, retaining course-derived rather than printed-example attribution.

The source explicitly contrasts polyhedral regions from multivariate linear tests with axis-aligned hyperrectangles. Q008 identifies one oblique boundary and Q016 only the univariate case; neither tests intersecting multivariate decisions or their resulting region. Add an explicit two-test routing/region application with stated inequalities.

Current questions cover shape, stable-class scale, label order and normal support but not the forward/backward means/spreads or the separate data-generation and split seeds. Add an integrated block-index/distribution/code-flow trace that distinguishes a sampled value from its generating mean and preserves source axis conventions.

issues.claim: color == red displayed next to n-way categorical description
issues.qualification: The shown equality is binary; a separate multiway category test can have one branch per category.
The documented ccp_alpha parameter supports minimal cost-complexity post-pruning; it was added in 0.22.

issues.claim: min_samples_leaf described as a parent-node sample requirement
issues.qualification: The integer leaf constraint applies to each child of a proposed split; min_samples_split is a separate parent-node condition.

issues.claim: Root displays Stable despite equal class counts
issues.qualification: The label is tie-breaking, not a strict majority; plotted thresholds are rounded, not exact estimator values.

issues.claim: Cannot extrapolate and predicts last seen value
issues.qualification: Prediction outside input range is possible; mean-leaf predictions do not automatically extend a numerical target trend and need not equal the last chronological target.

issues.claim: Forest code and binary figure appear near the three-class fall example
issues.qualification: The snippet uses undefined X_train/y_train names and the plotted binary data are not the earlier three-class synthetic dataset; no exact plot reproduction is claimed.
Current official default is max_features=1.0, meaning all features; classifier default sqrt is distinct.

issues.claim: Forests outperform a single tree on all robotics benchmarks
issues.qualification: No all-benchmarks evidence is provided; applications and prototype advice are not deployment or safety validation.

additionalSourceQualifications: Reduced-error pruning description is not the definition of every post-pruning algorithm.
Bootstrap omission is an expected fraction, not a fixed count.
Randomized training does not guarantee all realized trees differ.
Positive affine scaling invariance is scoped to exact threshold ordering, not arbitrary finite-precision transforms.
mutations: Reviewer evidence, independent check/finalizer scripts, snapshot, reviews and handoff only. No author, bank, source or Git edits.
